propositions: Defect review identified duplicated computation logic appearing in 2–7 locations across the codebase; fixes landing in one copy leave their twins broken, producing families of 3–6 related tickets.
Each consolidation child must collapse one duplicated computation into a single shared module while preserving all pinned observable behavior verified by named regression tests.

A construct-uniqueness guard test must prove exactly one implementation exists per consolidated construct by scanning src/rebar for the conjunction of distinctive atoms or AST shapes, with explicit escape markers for legitimate exceptions.

Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3 as originally written measure proxies (tests-only-additions, net-negative-lines) that correct consolidation work legitimately violates; they require restatement to measure the actual guarantee (one implementation per construct) plus evidence.
The 23-child epic is functionally complete; close is blocked only by 4 acceptance criteria needing revision to reflect empirical outcomes and consolidation reality.
